## Answers

A1.1          | No trigger — a display-format convention applied wherever pace, hr, position or zone values are shown; reference table (see A3).
A1.2          | pace value, hr (heart rate) value, position value, zone value — the raw metric values to format.
A1.3          | Formatted display text: pace as "M:SS" + detached "/km" unit; hr as integer + detached "bpm" unit; position as "n/30" (no spaces); zone as "Zone n." Unit is always a separate, smaller, text-secondary element, never concatenated to the value.
A1.4          | gap: screen and area where these formats are applied are not named in this block.
A1.6          | Not applicable — no trigger; the formatting convention has nothing to turn on or off.
A1.7          | Not applicable — nothing is produced by a trigger; the convention applies each time a value is displayed.
A1.8          | Not applicable — no trigger to re-fire.
A2.text.1     | Exact patterns given: pace = "M:SS" + "/km"; hr = integer + "bpm"; position = "n/30" (no spaces); zone = "Zone n." Unit is always a separate, smaller, text-secondary element, never concatenated to the value.
A2.text.2     | gap: what the pace/hr/position/zone display shows when the underlying value is absent is not stated.
A3.1          | Four format types, exhaustive here: pace ("M:SS" + "/km"), hr (integer + "bpm"), position ("n/30"), zone ("Zone n").
A3.2          | gap: which screens or consumers use these formats is not stated in this block.
A3.3          | gap: not stated whether pace, hr, position and zone are the only metric types formatted this way, or what happens if another metric needs formatting.
A3.4          | gap: whether these format conventions can change after delivery, and what happens to already-displayed values if so, is not stated.
A4.1          | pace, hr, position, zone: not defined here — they designate values from elsewhere, this block states only their display format; "/km", "bpm", "n/30", "Zone n", text-secondary: defined here directly.
A4.2          | gap: whether pace, hr, position, zone (and the text-secondary style token) are described elsewhere or marked existing is not stated in this block.
A4.3          | "smaller" compares the unit's text size against the value's text size (other term named in the same sentence: "never concatenated to the value").
